body:
# Sourdough starter

The starter lives in a jar on the counter and is fed equal weights of flour and water every morning. It is ready to bake with when it doubles within four hours and smells of yoghurt rather than acetone. A starter that smells of nail polish remover is hungry, not dead.

# Espresso

Espresso is brewed by forcing water at nine bars through a compacted puck of finely ground coffee. Eighteen grams in, thirty-six grams out, in about twenty-eight seconds. If it runs fast and sour the grind is too coarse.

# Knife care

Hone before each use and sharpen on a whetstone every couple of months. Never put a carbon steel blade in the dishwasher; the detergent will pit it overnight.

# Tomatoes

Plant out after the last frost, bury two thirds of the stem, and water deeply twice a week rather than lightly every day. Blossom end rot is a calcium transport problem caused by uneven watering, not by a lack of calcium in the soil.

# Compost

The heap wants roughly three parts brown to one part green. It heats to sixty degrees within a week when the ratio is right, and turning it every fortnight keeps it aerobic. A heap that smells of ammonia has too much green.

# Frost dates

The last spring frost here is usually in the third week of May and the first autumn frost lands in late September, which leaves about a hundred and twenty growing days.

# Boiler

The pressure gauge should sit between one and one and a half bar when the system is cold. Below that, top up through the filling loop under the unit. It was serviced in October and the next service is due in October next year.

# Electrics

The consumer unit is in the cupboard by the front door. The upstairs ring main is on the third breaker; the kitchen sockets and the oven each have their own.

# Roof

The felt under the ridge tiles was replaced two summers ago. The gutters need clearing every autumn once the lime tree drops, or the downpipe at the back blocks and the wall below it stains.

# Lisbon

Stayed in Alfama, which is beautiful and entirely uphill. The tram is a tourist ride rather than transport; the metro is fast and cheap. Ate pastel de nata every single morning and would do it again.

# Packing

One carry-on, four shirts, two trousers, laundry every third night. Chargers and passport go in the same pocket every trip so there is never a search.

# Kyoto

Go in November for the maples and accept the crowds, or in February for the cold and the quiet. The bus network reaches the temples the trains do not.

# Standup

Nine forty every weekday, fifteen minutes, three questions each. Wednesday is skipped in favour of written updates because half the team is in another timezone.

# Incident review

Blameless, within two working days, and the output is a written timeline plus at most three actions with owners. An action without an owner is a wish.

# On-call

One week rotations starting Thursday morning. The pager escalates after ten minutes to the secondary and after twenty to the engineering manager.

# Running

Easy runs should feel conversational; if a sentence cannot be finished, it is too fast. Roughly eighty percent of weekly mileage belongs at that easy pace and the rest at threshold.

# Sleep

Same wake time every day, including weekends. Caffeine has a half life of about five hours, so an afternoon coffee is still a quarter present at bedtime.

# Physio

Calf raises three sets of fifteen, single leg, every other day. The achilles complains when the volume jumps more than ten percent in a week.

# Mortgage

Fixed until March, then it reverts. Overpayments are capped at ten percent of the balance per year without a penalty.

# Tax

Self assessment is due at the end of January and the payment on account falls at the same time. Receipts live in the paperless instance, tagged by year.

# Git

Rebase local work before opening a pull request, never rewrite a branch someone else has pulled. A commit message explains why, since the diff already explains what.

# Postgres

An index is not free on write. Check pg_stat_user_indexes before adding another, because an unused index costs every insert and buys nothing.

# Go

Accept interfaces, return structs. A goroutine without a way to stop it is a leak, so every long lived one takes a context or a done channel.

# Guitar

Change strings every couple of months or when they go dull. Practice with a metronome at a tempo that feels slow, then raise it by four beats a minute at a time.

# Cafes

The place by the water pours a decent flat white and the pastry counter has a sour cherry tart worth the queue. Coffee costs half what it does at home. Cash only before eleven.

# Shower

The mixer loses pressure whenever the kitchen tap runs, which is a flow problem in the old pipework rather than anything wrong with the unit itself. The bar valve was replaced last spring.

# Handover

The document lists who is away, who owns each service this month, and what is accountable to whom while the usual owner is out. Update it on the Friday before you leave.

# Insurance

Renews in June. Cancelling early costs a fee of thirty pounds, and the excess is capped at four hundred. Paying annually is cheaper than paying monthly by about eight percent.

# Logging

Every background job logs a start and a stop line with the same request id, so a worker that dies quietly still leaves a gap you can see. Structured fields, not sentences.

# Greenhouse

The glass wants a wash before the growing season starts or the seedlings stretch. Vent it on any day over twenty degrees, even in March, because it cooks in there.

# Recording

A condenser two feet back and slightly off axis, and replace the cable before blaming the room. Months of takes taught me the string section always needs more air than it sounds like it does.
